key_insight: AHP ranked plasma transferred arc welding (PTAW) as the best hardfacing route for NiCrBSi coatings, combining superior microhardness with the most favorable composite grade.
engineering_relevance: For wear-critical steel components, optimized PTAW hardfacing can extend service life and lower cost by improving coating hardness and metallurgical quality.
method: Compared five welding techniques using analytic hierarchy process (SMAW, MIG, TIG, automatic TIG, PTAW)
Hardfaced SS410 substrate with Colmonoy-4 nickel-based powder under selected process parameters
Characterized coating hardness and microstructure to relate performance to carbide/boride formation
evidence_signal: PTAW achieved 501.8 HV1 microhardness and a composite grade of 0.47, with microstructural evidence of hard phases such as Cr and Ni borides/carbides.
watch_item: The result is based on specific SS410 substrate, powder size, and parameter window, so transferability to other materials or scales needs validation.
paper_title: Integrated AHP and metallurgical approach: comparing welding techniques and characterizing NiCrBSi coatings in hardfacing
